reason: The cited evidence shows that VEC correlates with Tc in related HEA systems (E3) and that disorder can influence superconductivity (E4), but none of the passages directly demonstrate that lattice distortions in Ti-rich HEAs control electron-phonon coupling or density of states, nor do they provide data on Ti-rich systems outside Nb-Ta matrices. The key mechanistic link between Ti content, lattice distortion, and superconducting parameters is therefore unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Superconducting properties in Ti-rich HEAs are controlled by average valence electron count (VEC).
Large lattice distortions from atomic size mismatch modify electron-phonon coupling and density of states at the Fermi level.
VEC and lattice distortion together set Tc and Hc2.
Ti-rich HEAs will show modified superconducting behavior relative to Nb-Ta-based HEAs.
